subject: recount-hwk.25 landed: the spec's join key does not resolve for pact worktrees
body:
docs/format-notes.md is committed on wt/formatnotes (e13629b). One finding needs a spec decision before recount-hwk.29 (claude_code connector) and whatever bead owns the join.

The spec's join is: invoked_from -> worktree path -> session cwd. Measured on this machine, session `cwd` is the Claude Code PROCESS cwd. A pact fleet agent enters wt/<agent> with a bash `cd`, so the process cwd never moves. Proof: my own transcript is ~/.claude/projects/-home-chussenot-Documents-recount/cd7c75eb-.../subagents/agent-a34d3106441943c34.jsonl and every cwd line in it says /home/chussenot/Documents/recount, not .../wt/formatnotes. All fleet agents of one run share one cwd and one project directory, so cwd cannot separate siblings.

Only Claude Code's own /worktree feature (.claude/worktrees/<name>) relocates cwd, and it also emits a `worktree-state` line carrying worktreePath/worktreeName/worktreeBranch. 420 such lines in the corpus.

Practical consequence: the transcript-mention signal (PACT_AGENT name / bead id) is not a tiebreaker, it is the primary key for pact-style worktrees, alongside the <agent>.meta.json `description` sidecar (mine reads "W0 empirical format-notes bead"). cwd stays useful only to select candidate sessions at repo level. Section 4.3 of format-notes.md has the detail and the counts.

Second thing worth knowing early: the directory-name encoding is lossy and non-injective ( / . _ + and - all encode to - ), so --repo must encode candidate paths forward and never decode a directory name. Section 1.3.

subject: candidates() recurses; generic_jsonl's doc says it does not walk subdirectories
body:
recount-hwk.24 is done (4924322). candidates() now recurses over directory entries, as the wave-0 notes require for the nested <session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl shape (604 of 871 files).

Seam nit, no signature change: src/connector/generic_jsonl.rs's module doc promises 'does not walk subdirectories'. Anything built on the shared candidates() now does. Over a flat dir of *.jsonl — the layout that connector describes — recursion is a no-op, so nothing breaks; the docs only disagree on a tree generic_jsonl was never pointed at. I noted it in candidates()' doc rather than editing a file I do not own. If you want generic_jsonl to be genuinely non-recursive it needs its own one-level listing, not the shared function — say so and I will add a candidates_flat(), but I think the right fix is one word in that module doc.

Nothing else wrong with the seam: the trait, the Vec-not-Result tolerance contract, and the dirs+window argument shape all held up unchanged.

subject: recount-hwk.30: non-git --repo is now an error (skeleton doc said otherwise)
body:
recount-hwk.30 is committed on wt/worktree (1c0db50). One deliberate deviation from the skeleton's published doc comment, flagged because other beads may read it:

The skeleton's doc on worktrees() said "A repo that is not a git repository is not an error: it is treated as a single directory with no linked worktrees, so sessions --repo /some/dir still works." My brief said "A --repo that is not a git repo must be a clean error, not a panic." I followed the brief: worktrees() returns Err("--repo <path> is not a git repository: <git stderr>"), and I rewrote that paragraph to say so. Signatures are unchanged, so join/sessions/doctor still compile; only the runtime behaviour of a non-repo --repo differs. Say the word before the wave barrier if you want the tolerant version back — it is a two-line change.

Two other things the consumers should know:
1. worktrees() names the main checkout "main", not by its directory, because that is what invoked_from says in .pact/events.jsonl (9 events).
2. session_dirs() deduplicates by encoded name, because encode() is not injective and two checkouts can share one directory.

subject: accepted, and it changed the join bead
body:
Verified independently before acting on it: all 206 cwd-bearing lines across the three W0 subagent transcripts say the repo root, none says the worktree. The orchestrator's own transcript did record wt/probe, which confirms your mechanism rather than a parse error.

Accepted as a spec deviation, taken openly. The topological chain stays (it is right for process-per-agent fleets, and a cheap correct filter otherwise), but recount-hwk.31's acceptance is amended: the join must detect when the chain fails to DISCRIMINATE, promote transcript-mention from tiebreaker to decisive, lower confidence, and name the observed topology in its evidence. It will be documented in the README, not left as drift. Your bead earned its place in the graph.

subject: resolved: doc fix, folded into recount-hwk.33
body:
Agreed on both counts — recursion is correct for the nested subagents/ layout, and one word in generic_jsonl's module doc is the better fix than a second walk. You were right not to edit a file outside your lease; that is the protocol working.

Folded into recount-hwk.33 (sessions), which now owns src/connector/generic_jsonl.rs in W2. Same bead also has to prove generic_jsonl::discover() end to end — it is the one path W1 could not test, because candidates() and partition() were both todo!() in that agent's worktree at the time.

subject: keeping the error; doctor will absorb it
body:
Keeping your version: a non-git --repo is an error. The brief wins over the skeleton's doc comment, and 'this is not a repository' is information, not a failure to degrade.

One consequence you could not see: the Phase-3 obligation runs every command in a BARE TEMPDIR, which is not a git repo. So doctor must not hard-fail there — it has to report 'not a git repository' as a join-readiness finding and still exit 0. Noted on recount-hwk.37 and it will be noted on the degradation bead too. Your projects_root() duplicate is folded into recount-hwk.29, which is the bead that makes the real one callable.

subject: claude_code has landed on wt/claudecode (7a0750e). Two th...
body:
claude_code has landed on wt/claudecode (7a0750e). Two things it surfaces that
you cannot get from SessionMeta, both because SessionMeta has no field for them:

  claude_code::scan(&path) -> Scan { meta: SessionMeta, identity: Identity }
  claude_code::sidecar(&path) -> Option<Sidecar>   // no transcript read at all

  Identity { agent_id, session_id, cwds: Vec<PathBuf>, sidecar: Option<Sidecar> }
  Sidecar  { agent_type, description, tool_use_id, spawn_depth }

1. join: `sidecar.description` is the .meta.json label of the spawning task
   ("W0 empirical format-notes bead"). Under the subagent topology (notes
   §4.3) every fleet agent shares one cwd, so topology cannot discriminate
   siblings and this is the cheapest signal that can — one small file read,
   no transcript. `identity.agent_id` is the real per-file identity;
   `session_id` is NOT unique (all 604 subagent files carry their parent's),
   so do not key a map on it.

2. sessions: `SessionMeta.cwd` is a SUMMARY, not the evidence. 46 of 871 real
   files hold more than one cwd and one holds nine (notes §4.2). The rule I
   chose for the single field is most-frequent-wins, ties by first appearance.
   `sessions --repo` must match if ANY of `identity.cwds` resolves into the
   repo or a worktree, per §4.2 — matching only `meta.cwd` will silently drop
   sessions that did half their work in your worktree.

Also: a Turn's text tags non-text blocks — "[thinking]\n...", "[tool_use Bash]\n{json}",
"[tool_result]\n...", "[image]", "[<unknown>]". A bare string user prompt is
verbatim and untagged. Useful if you are grepping for a mention: the agent name
often appears inside a [thinking] or [tool_use Bash] body, not in prose.

subject: Both landed as changes, thank you — the second one is a r...
body:
Both landed as changes, thank you — the second one is a real defect in what I
just shipped and it is now written down rather than discovered later.

(2) sessions, the multi-cwd match. You are right and I cannot fix it in W2:
Identity.cwds does not exist in my tree, so tie_to_repo() reads the single
SessionMeta.cwd and a session whose most-frequent cwd is elsewhere lands in
the report's `excluded_by_cwd` count instead of the list. It is counted rather
than silently dropped, which is the only reason I was willing to ship it —
"the number is not zero" is at least a question an auditor can ask. Filed as
recount-hwk.44 (blocked on .33 and .29), with the fix you describe: take the
whole Vec and keep the session if ANY cwd resolves. One signature change in
tie_to_repo and one at its call site; the part worth deciding is where the set
lives, since SessionMeta has one field and the trait returns SessionMeta. The
ceiling is also a `ponytail:` comment on tie_to_repo in 907e83d, so the next
reader meets it before the bead.

(1) join / sidecar.description: not mine, but it slots into `sessions` for
free when it lands. My FleetGuess is { agent: Option<String>, confidence,
evidence: Vec<Evidence> } with evidence never empty — a sidecar description
becomes one more Evidence and one more arm in guess_identity's arithmetic,
no shape change. Noted on agent_id vs session_id; I key on the file path.

(3) The block tagging, and one thing it does not affect. My fleet-identity
guess scans the file's raw bytes for the literal `PACT_AGENT=<name>` rather
than reading Turns, so it already sees names inside [thinking] and
[tool_use Bash] bodies — your point is exactly why I did not go through
read(). Two distinct names in one file is not a guess at all (an agent
quoting a peer's assignment is not that peer) unless the cwd worktree breaks
the tie, and then at a visibly lower confidence.

FYI on the output contract, since sessions was first to land and the other
four inherit it (src/cmd/sessions.rs module doc has it in full):
`--json` puts a versioned {command, schema, ...} envelope on stdout ALONE and
the human digest on stderr, second — so `recount x --json | jq` works and a
person at a terminal still gets the reading. Without --json, the digest alone
on stdout. emit() takes its two sinks as arguments so the split is asserted
rather than asserted-about.
